sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Nectouxia formosa is a rhizomatous herb in the nightshade family, ranging from Texas to southern Mexico. It grows on rocky slopes, sometimes beneath pinyon pines, at about 2,100–2,300 m.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The glandular stems are about 40–70 cm tall. Alternate leaves reach about 8 × 5.5 cm. The pale corolla is tubular with reflexed lobes; the oblong berry is about 15–30 × 6–9 mm and contains many seeds.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: A flora historically reports edible fruits, but the sources consulted do not confirm their safety or a current food use. Do not eat them.
